materials.title: Короткие ответы и усиление с do · B1
materials.text:
Teacher: Have you seen Ben today?
Learner: Yes, I have.
Teacher: Did you like the film?
Learner: No, I didn’t. But I do like the director’s other films.
Teacher: Why did you use ‘do’?
Learner: I wanted to make my opinion stronger.

materials.title: Короткие ответы и усиление с do · B2
materials.text:
Teacher: If someone asks ‘Have you seen Ben at all?’, how can you avoid repeating the whole question?
Learner: ‘Yes, I have, actually.’ The auxiliary stands in for the rest of the answer.
Teacher: How would you emphasise your opinion of the shoes?
Learner: ‘I do like your shoes. Where did you get them?’ I’d stress ‘do’.
Teacher: What if the question is ‘Did you like the film?’
Learner: Then I’d answer ‘Yes, I did’ or ‘No, I didn’t’.

materials.title: Короткие ответы и усиление с do · C1
materials.text:
Teacher: Does ‘I do like your shoes’ mean something different from ‘I like your shoes’?
Learner: The basic meaning is the same. The auxiliary adds emphasis, which can reinforce a compliment or contradict an assumption.
Teacher: How is that different from ‘Yes, I have’?
Learner: In a short answer, the auxiliary lets the speaker omit information already supplied by the question. It doesn’t automatically add the same emphasis.

materials.title: Помнить задачу или помнить действие · B1
materials.text:
Partner: Did you remember to lock the back door?
Learner: Yes, I did. I remember locking it before we left.
Partner: So you’re sure?
Learner: Yes. I remember checking it twice.

materials.title: Помнить задачу или помнить действие · B2
materials.text:
Teacher: What is the difference between ‘remember to lock’ and ‘remember locking’?
Learner: With ‘remember to lock’, I think of the task first and then do it. With ‘remember locking’, the action happened first, and I recall it afterwards.
Teacher: Use both in one exchange.
Learner: ‘Did you remember to lock the door?’ ‘Yes, I remember locking it right before we left.’

materials.title: Помнить задачу или помнить действие · C1
materials.text:
Teacher: Why does the infinitive change the meaning here?
Learner: ‘Remember to do’ is about remembering an obligation before acting. ‘Remember doing’ refers to recalling an event that has already taken place.
Teacher: Give an example where that distinction matters.
Learner: ‘I remembered to lock the door’ says I carried out the task. ‘I remember locking it’ describes the memory I’m relying on now.

materials.title: Фильм, мнение и вежливое несогласие · B1
materials.text:
Partner: What did you think of the film?
Learner: I liked the story, but I didn’t like the ending.
Partner: I thought the ending was good.
Learner: I see what you mean. I just wanted a clearer ending.

materials.title: Фильм, мнение и вежливое несогласие · B2
materials.text:
Partner: Everyone seemed to like the film. What did you think?
Learner: I liked the premise, but I didn’t think the ending worked. It felt rushed.
Partner: I thought it was surprising rather than rushed.
Learner: I see what you mean. My issue is that the characters didn’t have enough time to react.

materials.title: Фильм, мнение и вежливое несогласие · C1
materials.text:
Partner: Would you say the film earned its ending?
Learner: I see why it worked for some viewers. My reservation is that the final twist felt underdeveloped, even though the premise was compelling.
Partner: I thought leaving things open was part of the point.
Learner: Fair enough. An open ending can work well. In this case, I would have preferred a little more groundwork for it.

materials.title: Мои занятия и цели в английском · B1
materials.text:
Tutor: What do you like doing in your free time?
Learner: I like swimming, walking and building apps.
Tutor: What do you want to improve in English?
Learner: I want to speak more quickly and clearly. I also want to write better emails.
Tutor: How do you practise?
Learner: I take online classes and read aloud.

materials.title: Мои занятия и цели в английском · B2
materials.text:
Tutor: What makes a good English lesson for you?
Learner: I like having a clear task and enough time to discuss it with a partner. Then I want feedback I can use in the next conversation.
Tutor: Where will you use your English outside class?
Learner: I write to international colleagues and comment on videos. In live conversations, I’d like to form sentences faster and get my point across more clearly.

materials.title: Мои занятия и цели в английском · C1
materials.text:
Tutor: Could you give a specific example of what you hope to improve?
Learner: When someone asks an unexpected question, I want to respond without losing my train of thought. I’d also like to write concise emails that sound natural to international colleagues.
Tutor: What would good feedback look like?
Learner: I’d like the tutor to point out one recurring pattern, give a more idiomatic alternative, and let me use it immediately in another exchange.

Письменное задание
Turn the learner’s goals into a concise written request to a tutor. Include a speaking goal, a writing goal and a specific feedback request.

Напиши ответ по-английски, затем сравни его с примером.
materials.answer: I’d like to respond more fluently to unexpected questions and write clear, concise emails to colleagues. Could you flag one recurring pattern, suggest a more idiomatic alternative and give me a chance to use it straight away?

materials.title: Реакции и хвостики · шесть мини-реплик
materials.prompt:
Give a short interested reaction to 1–3. Add a question tag to 4–6.
1 I’m taking evening classes. 2 I’ve seen that film. 3 I didn’t enjoy the ending.
4 It’s going to cost a fortune, ___? 5 You haven’t met her, ___? 6 They liked it, ___?
Then read the answers aloud and try them at natural speed.
materials.answer: 1 Oh, are you? 2 Oh, have you? 3 Oh, didn’t you? 4 isn’t it? 5 have you? 6 didn’t they?

materials.title: Выразительное do и естественное несогласие
materials.prompt:
Rewrite four replies.
1 Make “I like your shoes” a stronger compliment. 2 Agree completely with “The ending worked.” 3 Disagree gently about a film ending and give a reason. 4 You didn’t hear the last part, so ask the speaker to repeat it.
materials.answer: 1 I do like your shoes! 2 I couldn’t agree more. 3 I see what you mean, but the final twist felt rushed to me. 4 I didn’t catch the last part. Could you say that again?

materials.title: Разговор с преподавателем · цели и конкретный feedback
materials.prompt: Tell a teacher one speaking goal, one reading or pronunciation goal, and one writing goal. Give a real example for each. Finish with a clear request for feedback. Then read your answer aloud once.
materials.answer: I’d like to answer unexpected questions without losing my train of thought. When I read aloud, I’d like feedback on word stress. I also want to write clearer emails to international colleagues. Could you point out one recurring pattern and give me a more natural way to phrase it?

materials.title: Материал предмета и изготовитель · made of / made by
materials.prompt: Choose made of or made by. 1 These shoes are ___ leather. 2 This chair was ___ a local carpenter. 3 The cup is ___ glass. 4 The film was ___ an independent studio. Then describe a real object using both forms.
materials.answer: 1 made of, 2 made by, 3 made of, 4 made by. The desk is made of oak and was made by a local carpenter.
